original_claim_or_option: C07: Route 457/459 schedules cluster on shared corridor
methodological_rationale: Empirical timetable verification confirmed that Route 457 and 459 depart Brooklyn Rd stops 2 minutes apart on Sundays followed by a 58-minute gap. The factual schedule clustering finding in F-108 is robust and mathematically accurate.

stage_3_corrected_rating: well supported as a scheduling improvement with operational rostering and contract variation dependencies (zero-cost claim refuted; schedule shift requires depot rostering)
methodological_rationale: Existing driver fatigue rules (Bus Safety Act 2009) do not inherently prevent shifting departures by 15 minutes; however, altering shift blocks requires re-rostering layovers and meal breaks under industrial awards, incurring contract variation costs rather than zero resource cost.
key_evidence_source: Bus Safety Act 2009 (Vic); Bus Industry Award 2020; S05, S06

original_claim_or_option: C11/C12: Tighter FlexiRide delivery standards at no cost
stage_3_corrected_rating: valid policy mechanism designed to expose microtransit cost failure; transition to fixed-route buses managed via operational decision frameworks and transparent costing (no statutory triggers required)
methodological_rationale: Imposing high service standards deliberately reveals the prohibitive per-passenger subsidy of microtransit ($35-$50), establishing an operational rationale to reallocate fleet and hours to high-frequency scheduled feeder corridors under DTP service frameworks without requiring statutory triggers.
key_evidence_source: Currie (2018); DTP FlexiRide trial; S04, S07

original_claim_or_option: C01: Stop proximity alone overstates useful access
methodological_rationale: Methodological critique that buffer-based stop proximity overstates access without considering frequency, span, and directness is fully confirmed by transport geography literature.

original_claim_or_option: C04: Network walking plus frequency/span captures access
methodological_rationale: Pedestrian network distance combined with service frequency standards provides an accurate access metric, reflecting actual walkability in outer suburban curvilinear street patterns.

stage_3_corrected_rating: well supported for acute 6-month temporary shock relief; weak mechanism for structural poverty (>50% rent-to-income); requires screening for formal VCAT possession listings to maximize crisis targeting efficiency
methodological_rationale: Causal evidence confirms cash grants provide acute temporary liquidity relief. While non-entry into emergency shelters (82-90%) does not mean assistance is wasted—as preventing eviction preserves broader family stability—untargeted cash transfers exhibit substantial targeting inefficiency compared to screening for formal VCAT possession notices.
key_evidence_source: Shinn et al. (2013); Evans et al. (2016); Jacobs et al. (2020); S09, S11, S13

stage_3_corrected_rating: well supported for tribunal defense; qualified by repayment hardship risks and tribunal capacity bottlenecks
methodological_rationale: Legal representation significantly improves hearing outcomes; however, negotiated repayment plans under s 330A impose material financial hardship on statutory benefit recipients ($395/wk JobSeeker), creating secondary default risk under s 91ZM.
key_evidence_source: Greiner et al. (2013); VLSB (2024); RTA 1997 s 330A; S12, S15

stage_3_corrected_rating: better alternative in theory; unfeasible as immediate eviction diversion due to 17-month priority waitlists and 3% total stock deficit
methodological_rationale: Social housing offers durable long-term stability (>92% retention), but treating it as an agile crisis diversion mechanism is unfeasible given severe stock shortages and multi-month waitlists.

original_claim_or_option: A08: Unit economics and fiscal offsets
stage_3_corrected_rating: well supported for social welfare and congestion reductions; unsupported as a cashable Treasury dividend
methodological_rationale: Research correction to F-113: averted emergency department presentations and court listings represent broader economic and societal welfare benefits (non-cashable capacity offsets), not cash revenues that flow into the state budget. No adopted policy claimed these as cashable revenue.
key_evidence_source: Victorian Budget 2026-27 BP2; DTF VGR Guidelines; S18

original_claim_or_option: A01: Baseline homelessness scale and VCAT listing volume
methodological_rationale: Official data on Specialist Homelessness Services clients (AIHW 2024) and VCAT residential tenancies dispute volume (26,500 matters) verified as methodologically sound and accurate.
key_evidence_source: AIHW (2024); VCAT Annual Report 2023-24; S08, S15

methodological_rationale: Causal evidence confirms that formal eviction causes severe negative externalities including employment loss, emergency shelter entry, mental health decompensation, and debt default.
